ash: Heads-up: noticed ~22 small-gang jobs Pending in ap-southeast1 after a node reimage. All request 1gpu. Scheduler is leaving 1-GPU islands across NVLink domains. Anyone seen NVLink-aware packing issues?
nina: Yup. We have a mix of node SKUs where NVLink groups GPUs into two islands per machine. Our topology plugin doesn't consider NVLink domain boundaries, so it counts free GPUs but can't satisfy gang-affinity for multi-gpu jobs and ends up scattering 1gpu jobs to avoid filling an island.
pete: `kubectl describe` shows failures: "0/48 nodes are available: 18 node(s) had unfulfilled topologySpreadConstraints, 12 node(s) had taint {gpu.warm=true:NoSchedule}". Also saw a spike in pod preemptions when scheduler tried to consolidate across NVLink domains.
ash: sched-bot: suggestion -> short term: relax topologySpreadConstraint to Prefer for best-effort tiny-gang; add toleration for gpu.warm on low-priority queue; enable scheduler batching window 3m to coalesce small requests.
nina: Agreed. Additional short fix: run descheduler job to evict tiny best-effort pods from partially-filled nodes so they can backfill properly (cron every 10m). Risk: brief extra evictions.
pete: Long-term: extend topology-aware scoring to include NVLink domain as topologyKey (e.g., node.alpha/nvlink-domain) and prefer packing inside domains for gang jobs, while still spreading racks for redundancy. That requires node labeling from hw-inventory and a scheduler scoring plugin change.
ash: Canaries: patch low-priority deployment in ap-southeast1 only: add toleration and change spread to Prefer. Will roll 10 pods, watch packing_hole_rate and p99_schedule_latency for 10m. If eviction_rate > 15/min rollback.
ash: Applying now.
sched-bot: predicted cost delta +0.3% reserved utilization, predicted SLO improvement ~4%.
